cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: CAP says that during a network partition, a distributed data store must choose between Consistency (every read sees the latest write or errors) and Availability (every request gets an answer, possibly stale). Partitions cannot be ruled out.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: So the real choice is CP or AP behaviour during a partition, chosen per use case: CP for balances, locks and leader election; AP for feeds, carts and counters. PACELC extends CAP to the latency vs consistency trade-off when there is no partition.

questions.q: Can you pick a CA distributed database?
questions.a: No. CA describes a system that never has partitions, which in practice is a single node.
